references.text: Moses goes up a high mountain, Mount Sinai, where he receives the law from God, parallel to how Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain.

Isaiah prophesies about a servant who will grow up before the Lord like a tender shoot, having no beauty or majesty. This can be seen in connection with Jesus' transfiguration and the revelation of his divine nature.
Malachi prophesies about the coming day of the Lord, when the Lord himself will come to his temple. This can be viewed as a precursor to Jesus' transfiguration and the revelation of his divinity.
Matthew's version of the transfiguration on the mountain, which is a direct parallel to the event described in Mark 9:2.
Luke's description of the transfiguration, which presents a parallel account to Mark 9:2.
John describes the Word who became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory. This provides insight into Jesus' divine nature, also revealed in the transfiguration.
The book of Hebrews compares Jesus with Moses, highlighting Jesus' superiority and divine glory, which is also revealed in the transfiguration.
Revelation describes Jesus with a face shining like the sun in all its power, reminiscent of Jesus' transformed appearance during the transfiguration.
